newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico May revised trade surplus $220 million.
newsitem.headline: Mexico May revised trade surplus $220 million.

text.p: Mexico's revised trade surplus for May was $220 million, the Finance Ministry said on Thursday.
Exports in May were $8.811 billion, while imports were $8.591 billion, it said.

The trade surplus in May was originally reported at $88 million, but the finance ministry said the main corrections were due to changes in the maquiladora and automotive industries as well as exports from the agriculture sector.
A survey of 13 Mexican brokerage houses and research firms by Reuters found average expectations of a surplus of $158.98 million in May.
The revised April trade surplus was $50 million.

Petroleum exports were 10.4 percent of total exports in May. Of the non-petroleum exports, manufacturing made up 85.3 percent of that total, while agricultural products were 3.8 percent. Other mining exports made up 0.5 percent.
Exports of manufactured products were $7.516 billion in May, up 11.9 percent on the year.
Exports from the petroleum sector were $917 million, down 2.7 percent from the same month a year earlier.
Agricultural product exports were $337 million, down 9.2 percent from May in 1996.
Of the imports, intermediate goods were $6.731 billion in May, 11.0 percent higher than in the same month a year earlier, it said.
Imports of capital goods rose 31.8 percent to $1.207 billion in May from the same month a year earlier, it said.
Imports of consumer goods rose 29.6 percent to $653 million in May from the same month a year earlier.
The ministry said the accumulated trade surplus for the five months totaled $1.784 billion.
In the first five months, exports totaled $43.00 billion, 13.6 percent higher than in the same period a year earlier, it said.
It said that for the first five months, imports were $41.216 billion, which rose 19.5 percent over the same period a year earlier.
